_comment: Canonical display-name cases, shared by all three implementations.
The rule 'what is this star called?' was implemented four times -- PHP
(StarFormatter::getDisplayName), the API twice (StarBase and StarDetail), and React
(getStarDisplayName) -- and they disagreed. This file is the single source of truth
they lacked. It is mounted into every test container at /fixtures (see the Makefile).
CANONICAL ORDER, decided by the maintainer 2026-07-29 (DISPLAY-NAME-CANON):
fictional name (only when world_id > 0)
proper
bayer + con      (both required; trimmed)
flam + con       (both required; trimmed)
GJ               <- Gliese-Jahreiss first: this is a map of the solar
HD                  neighbourhood, so the nearby-star catalog is the most
HIP                 useful identifier to show. The API and React previously
HR                  led with HIP, which favours bright stars.
CNS5
TYC
Gaia
spect            (informative for an anonymous star)
ID <id>          (last resort, so a name is never empty)
If a case here has a 'world_id' key, pass it to the implementation; otherwise 0.

cases.name: bayer plus constellation when there is no proper name
flamsteed plus constellation when there is no bayer
bayer without a constellation cannot form a name and falls through
cases.note: PHP used to return 'Alp ' with a trailing space. A bayer letter needs its constellation to form a name.

cases.name: yale bright star only
cases.note: PHP had no hr branch at all and returned an empty string; StarDetail returned 'ID 7'. Both fixed.

cases.name: star 7301: gj and hip both present -- the real divergence
cases.note: The row that exposed the original bug. GJ-first is the canonical order, so GJ 1 is correct and the API's old HIP 439 was wrong.

cases.name: empty strings are not names
cases.note: The catalog contains empty strings as well as nulls; both must fall through.

cases.name: leading whitespace in bayer is trimmed
cases.note: The source data carries padding. All three stacks now trim.

cases.name: spectral type is the last informative fallback
cases.note: Better than a bare database id for an otherwise anonymous star.

cases.name: a star with nothing at all still gets a name
cases.note: Guarantees the name is never empty. PHP used to return '' here.

cases.name: fictional name wins over the proper name when a world is selected
cases.note: The API ignored the fictional name entirely, which is why PHP forked the whole chain.

cases.name: fictional name is ignored when no world is selected
